content: Carboxymethyl cellulose is an ophthalmologic agent that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of symptoms such as burning, irritation, and discomfort caused by dryness of the eye. Common side effects associated with its use include eye pain, changes in vision, and irritation of the eye. It may also serve as a protective agent against further irritation. The recommended dosage involves instilling one or two drops into the affected eye(s) as needed. The container should be discarded after use. For post-operative dryness and discomfort, such as after LASIK surgery, patients should follow the specific instructions provided by their eye doctor. There is limited information available regarding the off-label use of carboxymethyl cellulose in both adult and pediatric populations. Similarly, there is no detailed guidance on its use in pediatric patients, including FDA-labeled or off-label indications. The drug is contraindicated for external use only. To prevent contamination, users should avoid touching the tip of the container to any surface, including the eye itself. The solution should not be reused, and the container must be discarded after opening. If the solution changes color or becomes cloudy, it should not be used. Patients are advised to discontinue use and consult a doctor if they experience eye pain, changes in vision, persistent redness or irritation, or if symptoms worsen or persist for more than 72 hours. The product should be kept out of reach of children, and in the event of accidental ingestion, medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center is recommended. Adverse reactions reported during clinical trials include eye pain, changes in vision, and irritation of the eye. There is limited information regarding post-marketing experiences, drug interactions, and specific population use, including during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing, pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, and immunocompromised patients. The active ingredient in this medication is carboxymethylcellulose sodium (CMC) at a concentration of 0.5%, which acts as an eye lubricant. Inactive ingredients include calcium chloride, magnesium chloride, potassium chloride, purified water, sodium chloride, and sodium lactate. Hydrochloric acid and/or sodium hydroxide may also be present to adjust the pH of the solution. The medication is administered topically to the eye. There is no specific information available regarding its mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, nonclinical toxicology, or clinical studies. Storage information is also not provided in the drug label. Patients should be counseled on proper usage, including avoiding contamination and discarding the container after use. The interaction between alcohol and carboxymethyl cellulose has not been established, and patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while using this medication. The brand name for this product is CARBOXYMETHYLCELLULOSE SODIUM®. There is no information available regarding look-alike drug names, drug shortage status, or pricing.
